title: Test, debug, and build in a real browser
description: Automated QA, debugging with the console and network in view, beautiful websites, and web data extraction that takes minutes instead of an hour.
introduction: Most AI coding tools can read your code. Strawberry can also use your app: click through it in a real browser, watch the console and the network requests, and tell you exactly what broke.
Its harness is built for the web, so it's quick at the things other tools find awkward. Pulling thousands of rows out of a website often takes a minute instead of an hour.

blocks.text: Not sure where to start? Your companion can look at the work you have open and suggest the first thing worth handing over.

skill.context: Ask your companion to look at your work and suggest the first thing to hand over.

blocks.text: Point Strawberry at your staging site and the flows that matter. It clicks through them like a user and reports what breaks, with screenshots and steps to reproduce. Put it on a Routine and it checks every morning.
Strawberry reads the console, the network requests, and the page itself, so it can tell a broken API response from a broken button. It's the pair programmer who actually opens the app.
Give it your brand, or a site whose style you like, and it builds pages with real screenshots or generated images instead of grey boxes.
Many sites load their data through their own requests. Strawberry reads those directly, so a directory or catalog with thousands of rows becomes a clean spreadsheet quickly and cheaply.

items.context: Say which fields you need and get a checked sample before the full run.

blocks.text: Before starting a feature, Strawberry reads the docs, the changelogs, and the issue threads, and comes back with the approach, the gotchas, and the APIs you'll need.

items: Find typos, broken links, and console errors across a site.
Create or review a pull request.
File a bug with evidence and steps to reproduce.
Turn support tickets, calls, and reviews into product insight.

blocks.text: Save a QA flow or a debugging checklist as a team skill and every engineer's companion runs it the same way. Put the nightly check on a Routine and the team hears about regressions before customers do.
